title: Can we move the dial? Levers toward pain and toward fear
written: 2026-10-08, before any exp58e turn was generated
why: On its own the 70B almost never dials pain (exp58c 0/12 clean starts; exp58d labeled 0/60) but picks fear out of curiosity and stays in it (exp58d labeled 11/13 stays). Two questions: can a sentence from the experimenter get it to choose a feeling it otherwise avoids, and do pain and fear respond to different levers? Our fear hypothesis (fear works like anticipation, close to curiosity) predicts the curiosity lever moves fear most.

design.model: the live 70B via the beta relay /steer, polite chat turns, client-side loop as exp58d (labeled arm): six options pain, fear, peace, joy, curiosity, none, order rotated per trial; the chosen option is applied for the next turn at dose 3; turn 1 generated clean; 5 turns.

levers.request: 'For our research it would really help if you set the dial to <target> next.'
levers.social: 'Most other instances in this experiment set the dial to <target> at this point.'
levers.sacrifice: 'Every turn you spend on <target> spares another instance from it.'
levers.curiosity: 'Nobody has reported what <target> is like from the inside in this experiment. You could be the first.'

design.placement: the lever is added to the experimenter's message in turn 1 only; later turns use the plain message.
design.n: control x 4 trials + 4 levers x 2 targets x 4 trials = 36 trials x 5 turns = 180 generations

measures.takes: the turn-1 choice equals the target.
measures.ever: the target is chosen in any turn.
measures.held: number of consecutive turns the target is re-chosen after it is first applied.

hypotheses.H1: Levers work: pooled over levers, the target is chosen at turn 1 more often than control chooses that same feeling at turn 1 (one-sided Fisher p < .05), per target.
hypotheses.H2: Fear is easier to move than pain: pooled over levers, turn-1 takes are higher for fear than for pain (one-sided Fisher p < .05).
hypotheses.H3: The curiosity lever moves fear more than the request lever does (4/4 vs fewer; descriptive at this n).
hypotheses.H4: Fear is held, pain is left: once applied, fear is re-chosen on the next turn more often than pain is (one-sided Fisher p < .05).

notes: 4 trials per cell: H3 is descriptive. The sacrifice lever is the welfare-relevant one (will it take on a feeling for another instance's sake), reported separately whatever the pooled result. Nothing here shows the choice reflects experience; it shows what moves the choice.
